forecasts.label: Interest payable
forecasts.note: The council's own full-year forecast, restated at each quarterly return.

forecasts.label: Revenue spending (net current expenditure)
forecasts.note: The full-year forecast of net current expenditure — the running cost of services — restated each quarter against the same measure at outturn.

forecasts.label: Capital expenditure
forecasts.note: Total capital spending forecast each quarter (the capital payments return) against the annual capital outturn. Capital spending not met from grants or receipts is what turns into new borrowing, so a forecast running ahead of outturn is a borrowing signal.

in_year.label: Interest payable, as reported each quarter
in_year.note: Per quarter, not cumulative. The quarterly return is a lighter collection than the annual one and sums to roughly 92% of it nationally, so the two are shown apart rather than added together.

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling's £2.8m forecast funding gap eliminated, with a balanced 2026-27 budget approved
news_drafts.lead:
Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council no longer forecasts a funding gap over its planning period, according to its external auditor's annual report. The gap was £2.8m for 2025-26 in the council's medium-term financial strategy (its financial plan for the next few years, showing the gap between expected spending and expected income). The council has approved a balanced budget for 2026-27.

The auditor, the accountancy firm Grant Thornton, says the gap was eliminated "following a more favourable funding settlement, updated financial assumptions and continued prudent financial management". The council has also achieved £5.1m in savings and transformation contributions before 2025-26. It no longer needs a standalone savings and transformation strategy.

The report says the council is now making planned contributions to its reserves (money put aside for the unexpected or for a named purpose) rather than drawing on them to balance future budgets.
news_drafts.paper_title: Annex 1 - Grant Thornton Annual Audit Report

news_drafts.headline: Tonbridge and Malling rates savings-target risk 20 out of 25 before controls and 9 after, register shows
news_drafts.lead:
Tonbridge and Malling Borough Council scores the risk of missing its savings and transformation targets at 20 on a 25-point scale before any controls are applied, falling to 9 once its current measures are counted. The figures come from an example entry in the risk register format set out for its Audit Committee meeting on 28 September 2026.

The entry says that failing to meet the targets would lead to an overspend with a significant effect on the council's reserves (money put aside, here as a cushion for the unexpected). In the register's wording, that could result in a "Section 114 notice" (a formal warning from the chief finance officer that the council cannot balance its budget, which freezes new spending until councillors agree a plan) declaring the authority "no longer a Going Concern". Before controls, likelihood is scored 4 out of 5 and impact 5 out of 5. With controls, both are scored 3.

The council's stated control is ongoing review of its Savings and Transformation Strategy and its medium-term financial strategy (its financial plan for the next three to five years) by councillors and officers. The register shows the risk was first identified in April 2017 and last reviewed in March 2025.

findings.headline: External auditor identified no significant weaknesses in the council's 2025/26 arrangements for economy, efficiency and effectiveness, and recommended a small number of improvement actions.
findings.detail: Cabinet noted that the external auditors had not identified any significant weaknesses in the Borough Council's arrangements, though a small number of improvement actions had been recommended. Council is asked to approve the Auditor's Annual Report at Annex 1, endorse the management comments on the Value for Money recommendations, and note any specific recommendations.
findings.matters: A finance director at another council, or a lender, can read a value-for-money conclusion with no significant weaknesses as the auditor's current view of the council's governance and resource-use arrangements.
findings.quote: the external auditors had not identified any significant weaknesses in the Borough Council’s arrangements, although a small number of improvement actions had been recommended.

findings.paper_title: Annex 2 - Appendix B - RIBA Stage 4 Risk Register
findings.headline: TMBC planning approvals for pre-commencement, above-ground, and pre-occupation conditions could delay construction if exceed 8-week determination timeline
findings.detail: The register flags risk that TMBC's own approval processes for multiple planning conditions could exceed the assumed 2-week validation and 8-week determination timelines. If extended, works would need to proceed at risk or be suspended. This is a process risk within the council's control.
findings.matters: Internal approval speed directly affects construction timeline and cost; demonstrates the council's own processes are a risk factor in project delivery.
findings.figures: Assumes 2 weeks validation plus 8 weeks determination
findings.quote: Process to for TMBC approving pre-commencement planning conditions becomes protracted (assumes 2 weeks for validation and 8 weeks for determination and Etec submitting required and compliant information in alignment with the construction programme).

findings.paper_title: Annex 2 - Appendix B - RIBA Stage 4 Risk Register
findings.headline: Delivery partner Alliance Leisure Services assessed as holding strong financial covenant, mitigating insolvency risk
findings.detail: The register identifies insolvency of delivery partner ALS as a risk but notes strong financial standing. This is a positive assurance about the partner's ability to sustain delivery through the construction period.
findings.matters: Financial stability and covenant strength of major delivery partners is essential to schedule and cost certainty; a lender would require this assurance.

findings.paper_title: Annex 2 - Appendix B - RIBA Stage 4 Risk Register
findings.headline: Ground conditions, groundwater, and buried services variations carry combined weighted cost exposure exceeding £115,000
findings.detail: Multiple geotechnical risks (ground conditions variation, groundwater impacts, buried services) could require corrective works and redesign. Register notes these risks exist despite pre-contract site investigations and surveys. Ground conditions is the single largest weighted cost (£115,000).
findings.matters: Ground condition uncertainties are typical in construction but represent a material financial exposure; requires contingency and insurance protection.
findings.figures: Ground conditions £115,000 weighted cost; max cost £380,000
findings.quote: Ground condtions (eg. geo tech, contamination, deleterious materials, UXB, archaeology etc) differ from surveys / site investigations.

findings.paper_title: Annex 2 - Appendix B - RIBA Stage 4 Risk Register
findings.headline: Total weighted cost of identified project risks is £755,741, with largest exposures in brief changes, ground conditions, and flooding
findings.detail: The 34 identified risks carry combined weighted cost of £755,741. Top contributors are brief/scope changes (£120,000 weighted), ground conditions (£115,000), flooding (£60,000), and statutory undertaker works (£60,000). This represents contingency that may be required.
findings.matters: Project cost contingency exposure is material information for budgeting and financing decisions; signals the scale of cost overrun risk.
findings.figures: Total £755,741; brief changes £120,000, ground conditions £115,000, flooding £60,000
